blocks.text: Revelation 10’s angel, open little book, and renewed command to prophesy can be read within Revelation’s wider reworking of Ezekielian imagery, including scrolls and related visionary scenes. This is an interpretive connection rather than an uncontested identification, but it highlights how Revelation develops familiar scriptural images in its own sequence.

Elsewhere, Revelation repeatedly reworks Israel’s Scriptures and organizes major judgment visions around sevenfold sequences of seals, trumpets, and bowls, with interludes and recurring motifs. This broader pattern helps locate the chapter’s seven thunders and its position near the trumpet sequence within the book’s larger literary design.
